en: to explain; to interpret; to comment

examples.en: An expert provides commentary on the game.
The teacher explained the difficult poem in an easy way.
At the museum, I met a guide who explained the paintings.

examples.ko: 뉴스가 끝나고 기자가 사건을 해설할 거예요.
examples.en: After the news, a reporter will give an analysis of the case.
I want to be a soccer commentator, so I'm studying.

examples.ko: 그 만화는 역사를 재미있게 해설해서 인기가 있어요.
examples.en: That comic is popular because it explains history in a fun way.

explain: 해설하다는 뉴스, 경기, 작품 같은 것을 전문 지식으로 풀어서 설명하는 거예요. 일상적인 '설명하다'보다 방송과 전시에서 더 자주 써요. 스포츠 방송에서 말하는 사람은 '해설자', 해설하는 글이나 말은 '해설'이라고 해요.

phrases.example: 해설을 들으면 그림이 더 잘 이해돼요.
phrases.en: If I listen to the commentary, I understand the painting better.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해설하는 말이나 글을 가리키는 명사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The noun for spoken or written commentary.

phrases.example: 그 해설자는 축구 경기를 재미있게 해설해요.
phrases.en: That commentator explains soccer games in an entertaining way.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스포츠 방송에서 설명하는 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The person who explains on sports broadcasts.

phrases.en: The teacher explained the grammar in an easy way.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 널리 쓰는 말이고, 해설하다는 방송이나 전시에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A general everyday word, while 해설하다 is more common in broadcasts and exhibitions.

explain_en: Give commentary on news, sports or art. 해설하다 is to explain things like the news, a match, or an artwork using specialist knowledge. Compared with everyday '설명하다', it appears more in broadcasts and exhibitions. A sports commentator is a '해설자', and the commentary itself is '해설'.

t90.ax: An expert provides commentary on the game.

examples.ko: 이 한자는 획수가 많아서 외우기 힘들어요.
examples.en: This Chinese character has many strokes, so it's hard to memorize.
I wrote slowly, counting the strokes of the character.

examples.ko: 한자 사전에서 획수로 글자를 찾을 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can look up characters by stroke count in a Chinese character dictionary.
I study characters with the same stroke count in groups.
The Korean letter for 'ga' has three strokes in total.

examples.ko: 이름 한자의 획수를 따져 보는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people consider the stroke count of the characters in a name.

explain: 글자를 쓸 때 한 번에 긋는 선을 '획'이라고 하고, 그 수가 '획수'예요. '몇 획'으로도 말해요. 글자를 쓰는 순서는 '획순'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: This character has many strokes, so it is hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글자가 복잡하다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say a character is complicated.

phrases.en: Please write following the stroke order.
phrases.nuance_ko: '획수'는 개수, '획순'은 순서예요.
phrases.nuance_en: 획수 is the count, while 획순 is the order.

phrases.en: How many strokes does this character have?
phrases.nuance_ko: 획수를 물을 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to ask about the number of strokes.

explain_en: Stroke count of a Chinese character. A line drawn in one motion when writing a character is a '획', and the number of them is the '획수'. You can also say '몇 획' (how many strokes). The order in which you write them is called '획순'.

examples.ko: 별이 하늘에 긴 궤적을 그리며 떨어졌어요.
examples.en: A star fell, drawing a long trail across the sky.

examples.ko: 야구공의 궤적이 휘어서 타자가 못 쳤어요.
examples.en: The ball's trajectory curved, so the batter couldn't hit it.
That politician's track record has been consistent.

examples.ko: 비행기가 지나간 궤적이 하늘에 하얗게 남았어요.
examples.en: The trail of the plane that passed stayed white in the sky.

examples.ko: 두 사람의 궤적은 대학에서 처음 겹쳤어요.
examples.en: The paths of the two people first crossed at university.
My job is calculating satellite trajectories.

explain: 물체가 움직여 지나간 자취나 길을 말하고, 과학이나 스포츠에서 자주 써요. '삶의 궤적'처럼 사람이 걸어온 과정을 비유할 때도 써요. 비슷한 말로 '자취', '흔적'이 있는데, 궤적은 선으로 그려지는 길이라는 느낌이 더 강해요.

phrases.example: 이 책은 한 작가의 삶의 궤적을 담고 있어요.
phrases.en: This book captures the path of one writer's life.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 살아온 과정을 비유해서 말할 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figurative phrase for the course a person's life has taken.

phrases.example: 카메라가 공의 궤적을 추적해서 화면에 보여 줘요.
phrases.en: The camera tracks the ball's trajectory and shows it on screen.
phrases.nuance_ko: 움직인 길을 따라가며 확인한다는 뜻으로 과학이나 스포츠에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means following and checking a moving path; used in science and sports.

phrases.example: 눈 위에 동물이 지나간 자취가 남아 있어요.
phrases.en: Traces of an animal passing by are left on the snow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 궤적보다 일상적인 말로, 지나간 뒤에 남은 흔적을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more everyday word than 궤적, pointing to marks left after something passed.

explain_en: Line a moving object leaves, like a shooting star or orbit. It means the path or trail left by something that moved, and is often used in science and sports. It is also used figuratively, as in '삶의 궤적' (the course of one's life). Similar words are '자취' and '흔적', but 궤적 feels more like a path that could be drawn as a line.

examples.ko: 놀이기구가 급강하하자 탑승객들이 일제히 비명을 질렀어요.
examples.en: When the ride dropped suddenly, the riders all screamed together.
The temperature is plunging, so dress warmly.
I screamed on the ride that drops suddenly.
The bird suddenly dove down when it saw food.
Hold the handle tightly in the steep-drop section.
I'm worried the stock price will drop sharply in the afternoon.

explain: 실제로는 '급강하하다'로 많이 쓰고, 기온, 비행기, 놀이기구, 주가처럼 갑자기 크게 내려가는 것에 써요. 값이나 인기가 내려갈 때는 '급락'을 써요.

phrases.example: 밤사이 기온이 급강하해서 아침이 많이 추워요.
phrases.en: The temperature dropped sharply overnight, so the morning is very cold.
phrases.nuance_ko: 날씨 뉴스에서 갑자기 추워질 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in weather news when it suddenly gets cold.

phrases.en: The airplane suddenly dropped sharply.
phrases.nuance_ko: '급강하하다'를 과거 해요체로 쓴 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past polite form of 급강하하다.

phrases.example: 급강하하는 비행기 영상을 보고 깜짝 놀랐어요.
phrases.en: I was shocked to see a video of the plunging plane.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 오는 명사를 꾸며 줄 때 쓰는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form used before a noun.
phrases.en_equiv: a plane in a steep dive

explain_en: In practice it is mostly used as the verb '급강하하다', for temperature, planes, rides and stock prices that suddenly fall a lot. For prices or popularity falling, use '급락'.

examples.ko: 이 나라는 석유 매장량이 세계에서 가장 많아요.
examples.en: This country has the largest oil reserves in the world.

examples.ko: 새로 발견된 가스 매장량은 얼마나 돼요?
examples.en: How large are the newly found gas reserves?
Coal reserves are gradually shrinking.
Experts are surveying the deposits of the mine.

examples.ko: 매장량이 많아도 개발 비용이 비싸면 소용없어요.
examples.en: Even with large reserves, it is no use if development costs too much.
Compared with the reserves, production is very small.

explain: 땅속에 묻혀 있는 석유, 석탄, 가스 같은 자원의 양에 써요. '매장량이 풍부하다/적다'처럼 말하고, 가게를 뜻하는 '매장'과는 소리만 같아요.

phrases.example: 그 나라의 석유 매장량은 아주 많아요.
phrases.en: That country has a huge oil reserve.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자원 이름과 함께 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing with the name of a resource.

phrases.en: This area has abundant coal reserves.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자원이 많이 묻혀 있다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say that many resources lie underground.

phrases.example: 이 광산은 매장량이 적어서 곧 문을 닫아요.
phrases.en: This mine has small reserves, so it will close soon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자원이 얼마 남지 않았을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when little of a resource remains.

explain_en: It is used for the amount of resources such as oil, coal and gas underground, as in '매장량이 풍부하다/적다'. It only sounds the same as '매장' meaning a shop.

examples.en: The cows are grazing in the pasture.
The pasture is wide, so it's good for raising horses.

examples.ko: 가뭄 때문에 목초지의 풀이 말라 버렸어요.
examples.en: The grass in the pasture dried up because of the drought.
The farmer took the sheep to a new pasture.

examples.ko: 이 근처는 예전에 모두 목초지였다고 해요.
examples.en: They say this whole area used to be pasture.
After passing the pasture, a green field opened up.

explain: 소나 양 같은 가축이 풀을 먹는 풀밭이에요. 일상에서는 그냥 '풀밭'이나 '초원'이라고도 하지만, '목초지'는 가축을 먹이려고 쓰는 땅이라는 점이 달라요. 농장, 목장 이야기에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 산 아래에 넓은 목초지가 펼쳐져 있어요.
phrases.en: A wide pasture stretches out below the mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 풍경을 말할 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing when describing scenery.

phrases.en: Every morning I let the sheep loose in the pasture.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가축을 풀밭에 내보내 먹일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when letting livestock out to graze.
phrases.en_equiv: to let out to the pasture

phrases.en: Horses run across the grassland.
phrases.nuance_ko: '목초지'보다 넓고 자연 그대로의 풀밭을 느끼게 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives a wider, more natural feeling than 목초지.

explain_en: It is grassland where livestock such as cattle and sheep graze. People may simply say '풀밭' or '초원' in daily life, but '목초지' specifically means land used to feed animals. It comes up often when talking about farms and ranches.

examples.en: This morning the temperature dropped below zero.
Today the temperature went over thirty degrees.
The mercury column goes up when the temperature rises.

examples.ko: 한파로 수은주가 뚝 떨어져서 두꺼운 옷을 입었어요.
examples.en: The cold wave made the temperature plunge, so I wore thick clothes.

examples.ko: 옛날 온도계의 수은주를 보며 열을 쟀어요.
examples.en: I took my temperature by looking at the mercury column of an old thermometer.

examples.ko: 수은주 눈금이 잘 안 보여서 안경을 썼어요.
examples.en: I couldn't see the mercury scale well, so I put on glasses.

explain: 뉴스에서는 '수은주가 떨어지다', '수은주가 오르다'처럼 기온이 변하는 것을 말할 때 자주 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '기온이 떨어지다', '날씨가 추워지다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.example: 갑자기 수은주가 뚝 떨어져서 패딩을 꺼냈어요.
phrases.en: The temperature suddenly plunged, so I took out my padded jacket.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제 수은 기둥이 아니라 '기온'을 가리켜요. 뉴스나 기사에서 날씨가 급히 추워질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It refers to the temperature, not to an actual mercury column. News and articles use it when the weather turns cold quickly.

explain_en: In the news it is often used as '수은주가 떨어지다' or '수은주가 오르다' to talk about temperature changes. In daily conversation people say '기온이 떨어지다' or '날씨가 추워지다' instead.

examples.ko: 이 셔츠는 빨간색 격자무늬라서 눈에 잘 띄어요.
examples.en: This shirt has a red grid pattern, so it stands out.

examples.ko: 창문에 격자 모양 틀이 있어서 집이 예뻐 보여요.
examples.en: The window has a lattice-shaped frame, so the house looks pretty.

examples.ko: 종이에 격자를 그리고 그 안에 글자를 써 보세요.
examples.en: Draw a grid on the paper and write the letters inside it.

examples.ko: 지도는 가로세로 격자로 나뉘어 있어서 장소를 찾기 쉬워요.
examples.en: The map is divided into a grid, so it's easy to find places.

examples.ko: 전통 한옥의 문에는 나무 격자가 들어가 있어요.
examples.en: The doors of traditional hanok houses have wooden lattices in them.

examples.ko: 노트가 격자 칸으로 되어 있어서 그림 그리기 편해요.
examples.en: The notebook has grid squares, so it's easy to draw in.

explain: 가로세로로 교차한 모양을 말해요. '격자무늬'는 붙여 쓰고, 옷이나 천 이야기에서는 '체크무늬'라고도 많이 말해요. 창문, 지도, 공책처럼 줄이 교차하는 것에 두루 써요.

phrases.en: I bought a plaid skirt.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷이나 천에 가로세로 줄이 교차한 무늬를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a pattern of crossing horizontal and vertical lines on clothes or cloth.

phrases.en: Old houses often have lattice windows.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나무나 쇠로 가로세로 틀을 짠 창을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a window with a crossed wooden or metal frame.

phrases.en: A checkered shirt suits you well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷 이야기에서는 '격자무늬'보다 '체크무늬'를 더 많이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: When talking about clothes, '체크무늬' is used more often than '격자무늬'.

explain_en: It describes a shape of lines crossing horizontally and vertically. '격자무늬' is written as one word, and for clothes and fabric people also often say '체크무늬'. It is used broadly for things with crossing lines, like windows, maps and notebooks.

examples.en: What is this car's engine displacement?
The bigger the displacement, the higher the car tax.

examples.ko: 제 오토바이는 배기량이 작아서 연비가 좋아요.
examples.en: My motorcycle has a small displacement, so its fuel economy is good.
I want to buy a 2000cc car.

examples.ko: 요즘은 배기량이 작은 차도 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: These days small-displacement cars are popular too.

examples.ko: 작은 배기량에 비해 힘이 좋아서 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was surprised at how powerful it is for such a small displacement.

explain: 자동차나 오토바이 엔진의 크기를 말할 때 써요. 보통 'cc'로 말하고, '2000cc급'처럼 '~급'을 붙이기도 해요. 자동차세나 보험 이야기에서도 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: Cars with a large displacement are powerful.
phrases.nuance_ko: 엔진이 크다고 말할 때 '크다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 크다 to say the engine is large.

phrases.example: 배기량이 작은 차는 기름이 덜 들어요.
phrases.en: Cars with a small displacement use less fuel.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작은 엔진을 말할 때 '작다'를 써요. 경차 이야기에도 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 작다 for a small engine; also comes up when talking about compact cars.

phrases.en: I want to buy a 2000cc-class car.
phrases.nuance_ko: '~급'을 붙여 엔진 크기의 범위를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding ~급 names an engine-size range.

explain_en: It is used for the size of a car or motorcycle engine, usually given in cc, and sometimes with '~급' as in '2000cc급'. It also comes up often when talking about car tax or insurance.

examples.en: I hung a large picture on the living room wall.
The building's wall was full of graffiti.

examples.ko: 이 방은 한쪽 벽면이 전부 책장이에요.
examples.en: In this room, one whole wall is a bookshelf.
Damp built up on the wall and mold appeared.

examples.ko: 벽면 색을 흰색에서 연한 파랑으로 바꿨어요.
examples.en: I changed the wall color from white to light blue.
Photos are hung on every wall of the exhibition hall.

explain: '벽'이 건물을 막는 구조물이라면, '벽면'은 그 벽의 겉면, 즉 보이는 쪽 면을 말해요. 그림을 걸거나 칠하거나 습기가 찬다고 할 때 '벽면'이 어울려요. 일상 대화에서는 그냥 '벽'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: I hung the photo on the living room wall.
phrases.nuance_ko: 벽의 보이는 면에 무언가를 걸 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when hanging something on the visible surface of a wall.

phrases.en: I painted the entire wall surface white.
phrases.nuance_ko: 벽의 한 면 모두를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the whole surface of a wall.

phrases.example: 건물 벽면에 큰 광고가 붙어 있어요.
phrases.en: A big advertisement is attached to the building's wall.
phrases.nuance_ko: 건물 바깥쪽 벽의 면을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for the outer wall surface of a building.

explain_en: The surface or face of a wall; more written and technical (벽면에 걸린 그림) 벽 is the structure itself, while 벽면 is its visible surface. It fits talk about hanging pictures, painting or damp. In casual speech people often just say 벽.

examples.en: The video plays automatically.
The internet is slow, so the music won't play.
The injured skin regenerated in a few days.
Discarded paper gets recycled into new notebooks.

examples.ko: 재생되는 동안 잠깐 화면을 꺼도 돼요.
examples.en: You can turn off the screen for a moment while it's playing.

examples.ko: 녹음 파일이 잘 재생되는지 확인해 보세요.
examples.en: Please check whether the recording plays well.

explain: 일상에서는 영상이나 음악이 '재생되다'일 때 가장 많이 써요. 재활용은 '재활용되다'가 더 흔하고, 피부나 조직이 다시 자라는 건 '재생되다'예요. 내가 틀 때는 '재생하다', '틀다'를 써요.

phrases.en: This file won't play.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영상이나 음악이 나오지 않을 때 일상에서 가장 많이 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way in daily life to say a video or song won't play.

phrases.en: The recorded sound plays again.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 번 나온 영상이나 소리가 또 나올 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a video or sound that already played comes on again.

phrases.en: When a wound heals, the skin regenerates.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸의 조직이 다시 자라는 뜻이에요. 영상 재생과는 다른 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Here it means body tissue growing back, which is different from playing a video.

explain_en: Most often it means a video or song 'plays'. For recycling, '재활용되다' is more common; '재생되다' fits skin or tissue growing back. When you start it yourself, say '재생하다' or '틀다'.

examples.ko: 작은 글씨는 확대경으로 봐야 잘 보여요.
examples.en: Small print is only clear when you look through a magnifying glass.
My grandfather reads the newspaper holding a magnifying glass.
In science class we observed leaves with a magnifying glass.

examples.ko: 이 확대경은 열 배까지 크게 보여 줘요.
examples.en: This magnifying glass enlarges things up to ten times.
I found an old magnifying glass in the drawer.

examples.ko: 확대경이 있으면 우표를 자세히 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you have a magnifying glass, you can look at stamps in detail.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 '돋보기'라고 더 자주 말해요. 눈에 쓰는 '돋보기안경'은 안경이라서 확대경과 달라요. 확대경은 설명서나 과학 수업에서 볼 수 있는 말이에요.

phrases.en: I read the small print with a magnifying glass.
phrases.nuance_ko: 확대경과 같은 물건이지만 일상 대화에서 훨씬 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The same object as 확대경, but much more common in daily conversation.

phrases.en: I observed the insect closely through a magnifier.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작은 것을 크게 해서 자세히 볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when enlarging something small to look at it closely.

phrases.example: 수업 시간에 확대경을 사용해서 잎을 관찰했어요.
phrases.en: In class, we used a magnifier to observe leaves.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과학 수업이나 설명서처럼 정해진 도구를 쓴다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Has the feel of using a set tool, as in science class or an instruction manual.

explain_en: Formal or technical word for a magnifying lens; not used for eyeglasses. In daily conversation people more often say '돋보기'. Note that '돋보기안경' means reading glasses worn on the face, which is different from a handheld magnifier. 확대경 is the word you may see in manuals and science classes.

t90.ax: I found an old magnifying glass in the drawer.

examples.en: You need to measure the sugar exactly before adding it.
While measuring the water, I misread the markings.

examples.ko: 계량하지 않고 감으로 만들면 맛이 매번 달라요.
examples.en: If you cook by feel without measuring, the taste differs each time.
We mix the herbs after weighing them on a scale.

examples.ko: 계량하고 나서 체에 한 번 쳐요.
examples.en: After measuring, I sift it once through a sieve.

examples.ko: 요리 초보는 재료를 하나씩 계량하면 편해요.
examples.en: For cooking beginners, measuring each ingredient one by one is easier.

explain: '재다'와 같은 뜻이지만 요리나 실험처럼 정확히 부피와 무게를 맞출 때 써요. 일상에서는 '재다'가 더 자연스러워요. 보통 재료, 가루, 물을 목적어로 해요.

phrases.en: I weigh the flour on a scale and put it in a bowl.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 '계량하다' 대신 가장 자연스럽게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural everyday replacement for 계량하다.

phrases.en: Please measure out just one spoonful of salt.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요리 설명이나 부탁할 때 쓰는 정중한 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite form used in recipes or requests.

phrases.en: After measuring the powder, I mix it with water.
phrases.nuance_ko: 순서를 설명할 때 이어서 쓰는 연결형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connective form for explaining the order of steps.

explain_en: Measure amount by weight or volume; cooking, industry, formal. It means the same as '재다', but is used when you need accurate volume or weight, such as in cooking or experiments. In daily talk '재다' sounds more natural. Its object is usually an ingredient, powder or water.

t90.ax: We mix the herbs after weighing them on a scale.
